name: Del Haskins
lines: *A big man in a flannel jacket climbs down from an idling rig and taps on the glass.
Evening! You're the new one. Name's Del. I been stopping here twenty years.
I'll take a hot coffee, if that thing's got any left.
payment: Two crumpled dollar bills and two quarters.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Tired eyes, kind wrinkles, a sunburn that stops at his collar. Very much alive.

inspect.label: Hands
inspect.text: Calloused. A wedding ring worn thin. He drums on the glass while he waits.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: His reflection in the glass is ordinary. It drums its fingers when he does.

inspect.label: SCAN
inspect.text: PULSE 88  TEMP 36.8°C  RESIDUE: NONE

talk.text: Twenty years? Anything weird ever happen here?
reply: Weird? Ha. Every stop on Route 9's weird after midnight.
Folks see things by the reservoir. Bus stop over there hasn't had a bus since before you were born, and I still see people waiting at it.

talk.text: Did you know the last attendant?
reply: Mara? Sure. Sweet girl. Always had a coffee ready for me before I asked.
Then one night I pull in and the booth's empty and the machine's still humming. Company said she transferred.
Transferred where, I said. They didn't say.
Funny. I was gonna ask you the same thing.
Feels like I've had this exact coffee before. Déjà vu. Happens a lot on this road.

lines: *The can thunks into the tray. Del pops it and breathes in the steam.
That's the stuff. You're all right, kid. See you tomorrow.
Huh. Not what I asked for, but I'll take it. Long road.
Out of coffee? Ah, well. Tomorrow, then.

name: College Student
lines: *A young woman in a university hoodie, keys in hand, phone at 3%.
Hi — sorry — do you have anything with caffeine? I've got four more hours of driving.
Energy drink, whatever's strongest.
payment: A card, then exact change when the card reader blinks ERROR.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Exhausted. Mascara smudged from rubbing her eyes. Nothing strange.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: Her reflection matches her. Though — when she turns her head, it seems to turn a fraction late. Probably the old glass.

inspect.label: SCAN
inspect.text: PULSE 102  TEMP 36.6°C  RESIDUE: TRACE (environmental)

cameras.note: Her reflection on the unit camera keeps looking at you after she looks away.

reply: Holloway. Mom's birthday. I'm going to be so late.

talk.text: Drive safe. Watch the reservoir curve.
reply: Ha. Yeah. My GPS keeps saying 'make a U-turn' around here. Like, constantly.

lines: Lifesaver. Seriously.
*She jogs back to her car. In the glass, her reflection is still standing at the machine. It stays there for a long moment. Then it walks away too.
Oh, coffee's good too. Thank you!
*In the glass, her reflection doesn't leave with her. It watches you for a while before it fades.
...Okay. Wow. Okay.
*She leaves. Her reflection stays a few seconds longer than she does.

name: Nurse Okafor
lines: *A woman in teal scrubs under a heavy coat. Her name badge says OKAFOR — KESSLER COUNTY GENERAL.
Evening. Something sweet, please. A chocolate bar. It's going to be a long one.
payment: Exact change from a coin purse.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Sharp, observant eyes. She's looking at the machine the way you'd look at a dog that once bit you.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: Normal. She avoids looking at it.

inspect.label: Badge
inspect.text: KESSLER COUNTY GENERAL — R. OKAFOR, RN — NIGHTS.

reply: It's always busy around three. People come in after three that... aren't meant to.
Sorry. Hospital humor. Ignore me.
Only when I have to. My mother used to say don't buy anything from the Kessler machine after midnight.
She said it like it was a joke. It's ten past twelve. I'm making an exception.

lines: Thank you. And — hey. Don't stare at the lot too long. It stares back here.
Close enough. Thanks.
Fair enough. Probably for the best.

name: Man in the Orange Vest
lines: *A lean man in a blaze-orange vest, flashlight off, steps out of the trees.
Batteries. Double A. Mine died on the reservoir trail.
Don't like being out there without a light. Not tonight.
payment: Four singles, damp from the trail.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Weathered. He keeps glancing at the machine's glass — not at you. At the glass.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: Normal.

inspect.label: Hands
inspect.text: He's holding the flashlight like a club.

reply: You ever hear the knocking? Out by the water. Like somebody tapping on the inside of a window.
My granddad said it started the year they pulled the bus out. Said they should've left it down there.
Coach 313. Went into the reservoir in '87. Thirteen people.
They never found all of 'em. Granddad said that's why they keep coming back to the stop.

lines: *He thumbs the batteries in. The flashlight comes on, pointed at the machine. For a second you both see something behind the glass — then it's just cans.
...Right. Goodnight.
That's not batteries. Forget it. I'll walk in the dark.
Then I'll walk in the dark. Thanks for nothing.

name: Girl with a Leash
lines: *A teenage girl in a puffer jacket holds a red leash. The leash ends in a collar. The collar is empty.
Hi! Can I get the peanuts? They're for Biscuit. He loves them.
Sit, Biscuit. Good boy.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Cheerful, cold-flushed cheeks. She's looking down and to the left, smiling, at nothing.

inspect.label: Leash
inspect.text: The leash is taut. It pulls, gently, toward the grass. There is nothing at the end of it.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: In the reflection, there is a small scruffy dog at the end of the leash, wagging.

inspect.label: SCAN
inspect.text: SUBJECT: PULSE 76, ALIVE.  SECONDARY READING (LOW, ~0.3m): PULSE NONE. TEMP 4°C. RESIDUE: HIGH. DISPOSITION: FRIENDLY.

cameras.note: On CAM 1 there is a small dog at the end of her leash.
The dog is on this camera too, sniffing the base of the unit.

talk.text: Cute dog. What breed is he?
reply: Mutt! Best kind. He got hit on Route 9 last spring but he's fine now. He comes back every night.

talk.text: It's late to be out walking.
reply: Biscuit doesn't like the daytime anymore. Neither do I, kind of.

lines: *She tears the bag and scatters a handful on the ground. The peanuts disappear one by one, with small crunching sounds.
Say thank you, Biscuit!
*Something unseen brushes against the machine. It is, unmistakably, a happy dog.
Oh. Biscuit can't have that. That's okay.
*The leash pulls her away into the dark, gently, like it knows the way.
Oh. Okay. Come on, Biscuit.
*The leash pulls her away into the dark, gently, like it knows the way.

name: The Drenched Man
lines: *The night is dry. The sky is clear. The man who shuffles up to the machine is soaked to the bone.
*Water runs from his sleeves and pools around his shoes. He smells like the reservoir.
...Water. Please.
It's so dry down there.
payment: Six quarters, dripping. Every one is dated 1987.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Gray skin. Lips blue. His eyes are clouded like a fish on ice. He looks at you with enormous, patient sadness.

inspect.label: Uniform
inspect.text: An old bus driver's uniform. The patch on his shoulder reads MERIDIAN COACH LINES. His name tag: W. PRUITT.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: His reflection drips in time with him. When he sways, it sways. It moves exactly as he does.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: Under the brighter tubes: the reflection is soaked too, and its mouth moves along with his. Perfectly in sync.

inspect.label: Coins
inspect.text: 1987 quarters. Wet. Cold. They smell of algae.

inspect.label: SCAN
inspect.text: PULSE: NONE.  TEMP 9°C.  RESIDUE: VERY HIGH.  DISPOSITION: TIRED.

cameras.note: CAM 1 shows him standing at the machine, dripping.
CAM 2 (unit camera) shows an empty spot in front of the glass, and a puddle that keeps spreading.

reply: Been better. Been a lot better.
I had a route. Nights. Kessler Flats to Holloway. I got everybody there on time for thirty years. Nearly.

talk.text: Why are you wet? It hasn't rained.
reply: It's always raining where I am.
Water, please. Just a little.
*He squints at you, water dripping from his brow.
...You. You were here before. Weren't you? Or will be. It's hard to keep track down there.

lines: *He drinks the whole bottle in one long swallow. Water runs from the corners of his mouth and doesn't stop.
...Thank you. You're kinder than the last few.
*He walks into the dark toward the reservoir. His footprints stay wet on the concrete until sunrise.
*He looks at the item for a long time.
...That's not water, son.
*He leaves it on the ground and walks away. The puddle stays.
*He nods slowly, like he expected it.
I'll be back. I'm always back.
*He walks toward the reservoir. You hear a splash, much too far away.

name: The Smiling Woman
lines: *A woman in a neat 1980s coat, hair set in soft curls. She is smiling. She keeps smiling.
Hello, dear! Isn't it a lovely night?
Strawberry gum, please. It's my daughter's favorite. Have you seen her? Little thing. About so high. Yellow raincoat.
payment: A shiny 1987 dollar coin. It is warm.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Lovely, symmetrical, friendly. She has not blinked since she arrived.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: Her reflection is smiling too. Its smile is wider than hers.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: With better light: her reflection's teeth go back much further than teeth should.

inspect.label: SCAN
inspect.text: PULSE: NONE.  TEMP: 31°C (rising).  RESIDUE: ABNORMAL — PATTERN UNMATCHED.  DISPOSITION: HUNGRY.

cameras.note: Not on CAM 2. But the gum slot, B4, is lit on camera as though someone is pressing it.

reply: Oh, that's all right. She'll turn up. She always comes to the machine eventually.
Children love machines.

talk.text: I'll keep an eye out for her.
reply: Would you? Oh, you're a dear. Tell me the moment you see her. The moment.

lines: *She takes the gum and holds it up to the light, still smiling.
Lovely. She'll come for this. They always come for the sweet things.
*She walks toward the bus stop and is simply not there anymore.
Oh, that's not right at all.
*Her smile doesn't change. She leaves.
*For one second, her smile drops completely, and her face is not a face. Then it's back.
Of course. Another time.
